# Digiwaxx

> Digiwaxx is a record pool and music promotion service operating since 1998,
> connecting artists' records to a network of 30,000+ working DJs (club,
> mixshow, radio, mobile), plus radio rotation, playlist placement, and
> published artist coverage. One-time campaigns: Starter $99, Pro $149,
> Elite $199. Main site: https://promote.digiwaxx.com, start at https://promote.digiwaxx.com/university.

## Promotion Services

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote

- [Independent Music Promotion](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/independent-music-promotion): Independent music promotion that rents you the label machine: DJ servicing to 30,000+ DJs, radio, playlists, and published coverage, while you keep 100%.
- [Music Promotion Service](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/music-promotion-service): Most promotion buys impressions. Digiwaxx sells access: your record placed with 30,000+ working DJs, plus radio, playlists and published coverage. No contracts.
- [Music Promotion for DJs](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/music-promotion-for-djs): What Digiwaxx offers DJs: a curated feed of new, DJ-ready records since 1998, and how DJs in the network shape which records break.
- [Music Promotion for Managers](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/music-promotion-for-managers): How artist managers use Digiwaxx: a repeatable promotion system per release, proof kits for pitching, and DJ data that guides booking and routing.
- [Music Promotion for Producers](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/music-promotion-for-producers): How producers use Digiwaxx: break records you produced, put instrumentals in DJ crates, and build the producer name DJs and artists recognize.
- [Music Promotion for Record Labels](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/music-promotion-for-record-labels): How indie labels use Digiwaxx: DJ servicing for the whole roster, per-release campaigns without per-release infrastructure, and reaction data for A&R decisions.
- [Promote My Album](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/promote-my-album): An album is a campaign, not one upload: lead single serviced first, the rest worked behind it across DJs, radio and playlists. $99 to $199, one-time.
- [Promote My EP](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/promote-my-ep): An EP gives DJs a choice, which is an advantage if you service it properly. Lead track first, the others behind it, to 30,000+ DJs. $99 to $199, one-time.
- [Promote My Mixtape](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/promote-my-mixtape): Mixtapes live or die in DJ crates. Get yours serviced to 30,000+ club, mixshow and radio DJs, with the versions they can actually play. $99 to $199, one-time.
- [Promote My Single](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/promote/promote-my-single): One single, one campaign: serviced to 30,000+ working DJs, pitched for radio rotation and playlists, with a Digiwaxx artist page. $99 to $199, one-time.

## Campaign Blueprints

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/campaigns

- [The 30-Day Post-Release Sprint](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/campaigns/30-day-post-release-sprint): A dated 30-day campaign for a record that is already out: packaging fixes, DJ service, a two-week content burst, and proof-backed pitching.
- [The 60-Day Release Plan](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/campaigns/60-day-release-plan): A full single campaign mapped week by week: asset prep, distribution timing, DJ servicing, the pre-save push, release week, and the two waves after. Copy it.
- [The 90-Day New Artist Launch](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/campaigns/90-day-new-artist-launch): Launching from zero: a 90-day plan covering foundation (profiles, sound, first record), first release with DJ service, and the second-release compounding cycle.
- [The Club Record Campaign](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/campaigns/club-record-campaign): A focused 6-week campaign to get a record tested and spinning in club rooms: packaging, DJ service, reaction harvesting, and converting spins into bookings.

## Release & Promotion Guides

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides

- [Afrobeats DJ Promotion: What Labels Need for U.S. DJ Servicing](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/afrobeats-dj-promotion-what-labels-need): A checklist for the label side of a U.S. Afrobeats campaign: what to prepare, what a servicing partner should do, and what to refuse to pay for.
- [Afrobeats vs. Amapiano Promotion: Different DJ Campaigns for Different Markets](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/afrobeats-vs-amapiano-promotion): One is a song format, one is a set format, and a campaign that treats them the same will underserve both.
- [Amapiano Promotion in the U.S.: DJs, Clubs, Mixshows and Diaspora Audiences](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/amapiano-promotion-in-the-us): A format born in the DJ booth breaks abroad through DJ booths. How a South African release actually reaches American floors.
- [From Lagos and Accra to New York, Atlanta and London: A DJ Promotion Plan](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/lagos-accra-to-new-york-dj-promotion-plan): A six week servicing plan for taking an African release into the diaspora cities, in the order the rooms actually work.
- [How Many Songs Should You Release?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-many-songs-should-i-release): Singles vs. EPs vs. albums for independent artists: the release cadence that builds catalogs, feeds algorithms, and doesn’t burn you out.
- [How Nigerian Artists Can Promote Afrobeats to DJs in the United States](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-nigerian-artists-promote-afrobeats-to-us-djs): The streams say Nigeria already won. The rooms are the part you still have to work, and the rooms belong to DJs. A practical guide.
- [How Shazam Works for Artists: From the Club Floor to the Charts](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-shazam-works-for-artists): A Shazam is a stranger hunting down your record seconds after a DJ played it. Why that makes it one of the most honest demand signals in music.
- [How Songs Break City by City: Viral Charts, Shazam Maps and Local Heat](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-songs-break-city-by-city): Charts are national but breakouts are local. How viral and city charts work, and why the ignition point is almost always a DJ booth.
- [How to Build Anticipation Before a Release](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-build-anticipation): How to make people care before your song drops: teasers that work, pre-saves, DJ pre-service, and the two-week countdown plan.
- [How to Get DJs to Play Your Song](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-get-djs-to-play-my-song): What working DJs need before they play your record: proper files, easy delivery, and the record pool system that reaches thousands of DJs at once.
- [How to Get More Playlist Adds](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-get-more-playlist-adds): The three kinds of playlists, editorial, independent curator, and algorithmic, and the realistic playbook for getting added to each.
- [How to Get Radio Play](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-get-radio-play): The realistic path to radio for independents: mixshows first, clean versions always, and the DJ activity programmers look for before adding a record.
- [How to Promote a Rap Song](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-promote-a-rap-song): How rap records actually break: club and mixshow DJs, record pools, radio, playlists, and content, in the order that works.
- [How to Promote a Single After Release](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-promote-a-single-after-release): Missed the pre-release window? The post-release promotion plan: DJ service, curator pitching, content waves, and second-wind tactics that work on live records.
- [How to Reach DJs With Your Music](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-reach-djs): The channels that actually reach working DJs, record pools, events, radio staff, and the outreach mistakes that get artists ignored.
- [How to Release African Music to U.S. DJs: Clean Versions, DJ Edits and EPK Requirements](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-release-african-music-to-us-djs): The unglamorous checklist that decides whether American DJs can actually play your record. Most campaigns that fail, fail here.
- [How to Release a Single](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/how-to-release-a-single): The full step-by-step plan for releasing a single as an independent artist: distribution, metadata, rollout timeline, DJ service, and release day.
- [Mixshow vs. Rotation: How Radio Airplay Really Works](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/mixshow-vs-rotation): The two-tier radio system nobody explains to artists: what a mixshow is, how spins get counted, and how records graduate to rotation.
- [Music Promotion for Beginners](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/music-promotion-for-beginners): New to promoting your music? The beginner’s map: what promotion actually is, the channels that matter, what to ignore, and your first 30 days.
- [My Song Isn't Getting Streams](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/my-song-isnt-getting-streams): Why your song isn’t getting streams: the discovery gap, the four causes, and the fixes that actually move plays, in order of impact.
- [Spotify Algorithm Tips That Actually Work](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/spotify-algorithm-tips): How the Spotify algorithm actually decides to push a song, the signals it reads, how to feed them legitimately, and what gets records shelved.
- [Streaming Numbers Lie, Rooms Don’t: The Music Metrics That Actually Matter](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/music-metrics-that-actually-matter): The effort test: metrics a listener has to earn, saves, searches, Shazams, repeat spins, beat any number that can be bought. Here is why.
- [The Best Day to Release Music](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/best-day-to-release-music): Friday is the industry standard release day, but the best day depends on your goals: playlists, charts, clubs, or attention. Here is how to choose.
- [The Data Trail DJs Leave: Spins, Crates, Charts and What They Tell You](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/dj-data-spins-crates-charts): Record pool downloads, detected spins and DJ charts are the earliest data in music. How each layer works and how to read a campaign report.
- [The Music Marketing Checklist](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/music-marketing-checklist): The complete music marketing checklist for independent artists, assets, profiles, pre-release, DJ service, release week, and post-release, in one list.
- [The Song Rollout Timeline](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/song-rollout-timeline): A week-by-week rollout timeline for an independent single: what happens at 6 weeks out, 4 weeks, 2 weeks, release week, and after.
- [What to Do the Day Your Song Drops](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/release-day-checklist-guide): Hour-by-hour release day checklist for independent artists: verification, links, content, outreach, and what to do that night.
- [Why Nobody Listens to Your Music (Yet)](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/why-nobody-listens-to-my-music): The honest reasons nobody is listening to your music yet, exposure math, trust signals, and the fixable gap between good songs and heard songs.
- [Why Your Song Stopped Growing](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/guides/why-my-song-stopped-growing): Streams flatlined after a good start? The four reasons songs plateau and the second-wave playbook for restarting momentum without re-uploading.

## Artist Goals

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals

- [How to Get Booked for Shows](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/get-booked-for-shows): How bookings actually happen for independent artists: the proof promoters need, the role of DJs and club records, and building a bookable package.
- [How to Get Club Plays](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/get-club-plays): What makes a record club-playable, how club DJs pick songs, and the service pipeline that gets your record tested in real rooms.
- [How to Get More Fans as an Artist](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/get-more-fans): Fans come from repeated exposure plus connection. The fan-building loop: borrowed audiences, capture points, and turning listeners into people who show up.
- [How to Get Playlist Placement](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/get-playlist-placement): The legitimate routes to playlist placement, editorial, curator, algorithmic, and how to spot the pay-for-placement scams that damage your profile.
- [How to Get Radio Spins](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/get-radio-spins): The spin-building ladder: college and community radio, mixshows, then rotation, and how DJ activity converts into reported spins.
- [How to Grow Spotify Monthly Listeners](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/goals/grow-spotify-listeners): Growing monthly listeners sustainably: the three inputs (catalog, external exposure, engagement), and why real-world play moves Spotify numbers.

## Straight Answers

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers

- [Can Independent Artists Use Digiwaxx?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/can-independent-artists-use-digiwaxx): Yes, most Digiwaxx campaigns are for independent artists. What you need, what it costs ($99 to $199 one-time), and what happens after you submit.
- [Do DJs Still Break Records?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/do-djs-still-break-records): DJs still break records, the venue changed, not the mechanism. How club, mixshow, and radio DJs turn unknown songs into regional and national hits.
- [Does DJ Promotion Still Work?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/does-dj-promotion-still-work): Yes, DJ promotion still works, and streaming made it more measurable. How club and mixshow play converts into searches, streams, and algorithmic pickup.
- [Does Music Promotion Work?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/does-music-promotion-work): Music promotion works when it buys real exposure to new audiences, and fails when it buys fake numbers. How to tell the difference before spending.
- [Does Radio Promotion Still Work?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/does-radio-promotion-still-work): Radio still reaches most adults weekly and converts to streams, legitimacy, and bookings. What radio promotion does in 2026 and how independents access it.
- [How Club DJs Discover New Songs](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-club-djs-discover-new-songs): Inside a working DJ’s discovery routine: record pools, DJ crews, floor intel, Shazam-and-charts, and where artist submissions actually fit.
- [How Do DJs Find New Music?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-do-djs-find-new-music): Every channel DJs use to find new music, record pools, promos, peers, digging platforms, charts, ranked by how much working DJs rely on them.
- [How Long Does Music Promotion Take?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-long-does-music-promotion-take): Realistic promotion timelines: what happens in week one, weeks 2 to 6, and months 2 to 6, and how long before a record shows real results.
- [How Many DJs Receive My Record?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-many-djs-receive-my-record): A Digiwaxx campaign services your record to a network of 30,000+ verified working DJs, club, mixshow, radio, and mobile. What that number means in practice.
- [How Much Does Music Promotion Cost?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-much-does-music-promotion-cost): What DJ servicing, playlist campaigns, radio pushes and PR actually cost, which to buy first on a small budget, and the spends that reliably return nothing.
- [How Record Pools Work](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/how-record-pools-work): What a record pool is, how music flows from artists to working DJs, what each side gets, and why pools have anchored music promotion since the 1970s.
- [Is Spotify Playlist Promotion Worth It?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/is-spotify-playlist-promotion-worth-it): Playlist promotion is worth it when it targets real, engaged playlists as one layer of a campaign, and worthless (or harmful) when it buys placements and bots.
- [Should I Pay for Music Promotion?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/should-i-pay-for-music-promotion): When paying for promotion makes sense, when it doesn’t, and the checklist your record should pass before you spend a dollar.
- [What Happens After You Submit Music to a Record Pool](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/what-happens-after-you-submit-music): The step-by-step of what happens after submission: review, packaging, servicing to the DJ network, pickup, spins, and the feedback that comes back to you.
- [What Is a Record Pool?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/what-is-a-record-pool): Record pool, defined: a membership service distributing new music to verified working DJs. Its 1970s origins, digital shift, and role in breaking records.
- [Will Promotion Increase My Streams?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/answers/will-promotion-increase-streams): How promotion converts to streams: exposure → searches and saves → algorithmic pickup. What to expect, what not to, and why bought streams destroy the loop.

## Comparisons

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/compare

- [Best Record Pools: How to Choose](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/compare/best-record-pools): The record pool landscape: what DJcity, BPM Supreme, and others do for DJs, what artist-side servicing means, and how to choose a pool for your goal.
- [Digiwaxx vs. Groover](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/compare/digiwaxx-vs-groover): Groover sells guaranteed-feedback pitches to curators, radio, and labels; Digiwaxx services records to 30,000+ US-rooted DJs. An honest comparison.
- [Digiwaxx vs. Playlist Push](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/compare/digiwaxx-vs-playlist-push): An honest comparison: Playlist Push runs playlist curator and TikTok creator campaigns; Digiwaxx services records to a 30,000+ DJ network. Different jobs.
- [Digiwaxx vs. SubmitHub](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/compare/digiwaxx-vs-submithub): SubmitHub sells per-pitch access to curators, blogs, and labels with guaranteed feedback; Digiwaxx services your record to 30,000+ DJs. Honest comparison.

## The Artist Journey

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/journey

- [“I Made a Song.”: Now What?](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/journey/i-made-a-song): You finished a song. The exact next steps: mastering, versions, artwork, metadata, ISRC, distribution, and lining up the people who will play it.
- [“I Need People.”: Building Your Amplification Network](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/journey/i-need-people): The people layer of music promotion: DJs, radio, playlist curators, blogs, and influencers, what each one does, in what order, and how to reach them.
- [“I Released It… and Nothing Happened.”](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/journey/i-released-it): No streams, no saves, no playlist adds after release? Why silence is the default for unpromoted records, and the exact recovery plan.
- [“I’m Getting Traction.”: Converting Momentum Into a Career](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/journey/im-getting-traction): The record is moving, now convert: bookings, complete royalty collection, publishing, performance rights, sync, and the next-release flywheel.

## Free Artist Tools

Index: https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools

- [Artist Bio Generator](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/artist-bio-generator): Free tool: enter your details and get three ready-to-paste artist bios, 1-line social, short streaming-profile, and full press/EPK versions.
- [DJ Pitch Generator](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/dj-pitch-generator): Free tool: enter your record’s details and get a short, professional DJ pitch, built on what working DJs say they want from artist outreach.
- [EPK Builder](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/epk-builder): Free tool: build a clean one-page EPK, bio, record, proof, links, contact, formatted the way promoters, programmers, and press actually read them.
- [Interactive Release Day Checklist](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/release-day-checklist): Work through release day without missing a step: 19 checks from final master to first-night momentum, ticked off in the browser with your progress kept. Free.
- [Press Release Generator](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/press-release-generator): Free tool: generate a properly formatted press release for your single or project, headline, dateline, quote, boilerplate, ready to send to blogs and media.
- [Release Budget Calculator](https://promote.digiwaxx.com/tools/release-budget-calculator): Enter your budget and release stage, get a recommended allocation across packaging, DJ service, content, and pitching, in priority order.
